### 3.2 Manual Promotion

In scenarios where automatic failover does not occur or additional verification is required, manual promotion can be executed by following these steps:

1. Put the Payment Gateway and Billing Service into maintenance mode to freeze writes. This prevents any data inconsistency during the failover process.
2. Confirm that the replica lag is under 5 seconds. This ensures that the data on the new primary is sufficiently up-to-date.
3. Run the command `ledgerctl promote --replica ledger-db-replica-1` to promote the designated replica as the new primary.
4. Repoint the DNS record `ledger-db.internal` to the new primary to ensure services can access the updated database instance.
5. Run the ledger smoke test to validate the functionality and stability of the new primary.
6. Take the Payment Gateway and Billing Service out of maintenance mode to resume normal operations.

- Audit Log Store

On March 27, 2025, Acme Corp experienced a Severity 1 incident involving a primary failure of the Ledger DB. The Ledger DB crashed due to a failure in its storage controller. In the event of a disaster, the Incident Response Policy (POL-COMP-003) will guide the response efforts. It is essential that all personnel involved are familiar with the protocol for reporting incidents and executing the recovery plan.
3.5 System-Specific Recovery Procedures
#### 3.5.1 Ledger DB Recovery
- In the event of a primary failure (INC-2025-012: Ledger DB primary failure), the Ledger DB recovery procedures outlined in SOP-OPS-014: Database Failover must be followed to restore services within the defined RTO and RPO. #### 3.5.2 Kafka Cluster Recovery
- For incidents involving the Kafka Cluster, such as Kafka consumer lag delays fraud scoring (INC-2025-008), the necessary steps from the Kafka Operations Guide (MAN-ENG-003) should be implemented to ensure data continuity and minimize operational disruptions. #### 3.5.3 Payment Gateway Recovery
- The procedures for recovery of the Payment Gateway, including handling payment latency spikes (INC-2025-031), will be based on the guidelines provided in the Payment Gateway Runbook (MAN-ENG-001). #### 3.5.4 Auth Service Recovery
- In case of incidents affecting the Auth Service, such as auth token validation failures (INC-2025-003), recovery actions must adhere to the architecture protocols set forth in the Auth Service Architecture document (MAN-ENG-002).
3.6 Communication Plan
A communication plan will be established to inform all stakeholders of the status of recovery efforts. The on-call engineer and Incident Commander will be responsible for relaying information to relevant parties in a timely manner.
4. Roles and Responsibilities

citations.title: Ledger DB primary failure
citations.snippet:
## Summary

On March 27, 2025, Acme Corp experienced a Severity 1 incident involving a primary failure of the Ledger DB. The Ledger DB crashed due to a failure in its storage controller. Although an automatic failover mechanism was in place, it did not activate because the health-check timeout was misconfigured. As a result, service disruption lasted for 34 minutes until the on-call engineer executed the manual promotion process as defined in SOP-OPS-014: Database Failover, restoring service to the Billing Service reliant on the Ledger DB. This incident highlighted gaps in our monitoring and failover configurations that require immediate attention.

3.4 Incident Response
In the event of a disaster, the Incident Response Policy (POL-COMP-003) will guide the response efforts. It is essential that all personnel involved are familiar with the protocol for reporting incidents and executing the recovery plan.
3.5 System-Specific Recovery Procedures
#### 3.5.1 Ledger DB Recovery
- In the event of a primary failure (INC-2025-012: Ledger DB primary failure), the Ledger DB recovery procedures outlined in SOP-OPS-014: Database Failover must be followed to restore services within the defined RTO and RPO. #### 3.5.2 Kafka Cluster Recovery
- For incidents involving the Kafka Cluster, such as Kafka consumer lag delays fraud scoring (INC-2025-008), the necessary steps from the Kafka Operations Guide (MAN-ENG-003) should be implemented to ensure data continuity and minimize operational disruptions. #### 3.5.3 Payment Gateway Recovery
- The procedures for recovery of the Payment Gateway, including handling payment latency spikes (INC-2025-031), will be based on the guidelines provided in the Payment Gateway Runbook (MAN-ENG-001). #### 3.5.4 Auth Service Recovery
- In case of incidents affecting the Auth Service, such as auth token validation failures (INC-2025-003), recovery actions must adhere to the architecture protocols set forth in the Auth Service Architecture document (MAN-ENG-002).
3.6 Communication Plan
A communication plan will be established to inform all stakeholders of the status of recovery efforts. The on-call engineer and Incident Commander will be responsible for relaying information to relevant parties in a timely manner.
4. Roles and Responsibilities
The following roles carry specific responsibilities in the implementation of this policy:
- The Owning Team: Responsible for maintaining the integrity of their systems and ensuring that necessary backup and recovery procedures are documented and tested.
- The On-Call Engineer: Tasked with executing recovery actions as outlined in this policy and related documents during incidents.
